title: Introduction to philosophy and ethics
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Read and write about core philosophical problems and the main ethical theories (consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics, contractualism), and apply them to questions such as punishment, privacy and professional duty.

weeks.1: What philosophy is: argument and method
weeks.9: Justice and the distribution of goods
weeks.11: Applied ethics: privacy, speech and autonomy

blocks.deliverable: Reconstruct a philosophical argument as numbered premises.
Write a short paper on whether free will is needed for blame.
Apply both theories to a rescue dilemma.
Week 7 midterm; compare two theories on a promise-keeping case.
Compare retributive and utilitarian views of criminal punishment.
Analyze a confidentiality dilemma facing a professional.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Ethics paper: write a 2,000-word paper defending a position on an applied question such as punishment or privacy, using two ethical theories and answering the strongest objection fairly.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
